title: (feat) Surface BMI reference ranges in the biometrics table
body: ## Requirements - [x] This PR has a title that briefly describes the work done including the ticket number. If there is a ticket, make sure your PR title includes a [conventional commit](https://o3-docs.openmrs.org/docs/frontend-modules/contributing.en-US#contributing-guidelines) label. See existing PR titles for inspiration. - [ ] My work is based on designs, which are linked or shown either in the Jira ticket or the description below. (See also: [Styleguide](http://om.rs/o3ui)) - [x] My work includes tests or is validated by existing tests. ## Summary Persists BMI as its own observation on the vitals and biometrics encounter so the backend can apply the concept reference ranges (including the criteria-based ranges landing in [openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo#63](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo/pull/63)) and sets the FHIR `Observation.interpretation`. Styles the biometrics table cells the same way the vitals table is styled today, so weight, height, MUAC and BMI all light up when out of range. - Adds a `bodyMassIndexUuid` config key defaulting to CIEL 1342. - Includes the BMI concept in the biometrics FHIR query and maps it to the `bmi` row key in `useVitalsAndBiometrics`. Keeps the client-side `calculateBodyMassIndex` fallback, gated on there being no stored BMI obs, so historical encounters still display a BMI value. - On form submit, pushes a fresh BMI obs whenever weight or height was touched; voids any prior BMI obs on edit. The calculation effect clears `computedBodyMassIndex` when either input is missing so a stale BMI is never persisted. - Renders biometrics cells via `NumericObservation` with the column's `conceptUuid` and the patient uuid, mirroring the vitals table. `NumericObservation` uses the backend-set interpretation when present and falls back to a patient-aware concept reference range lookup when it isn't — which means historical rows still get styled correctly. ## Screenshots BMI cell styled as `low` (peach background, down arrow) for a 28-year-old male with BMI 18 against the backend's BMI reference range (`lowNormal: 18.5`): BMI not computed or saved if one of the dependent values is not provided: End-to-end network trace showing BMI persisted as an obs on save: ``` POST /ws/rest/v1/encounter → 201 Created obs: - Weight (kg): 55.0 - Height (cm): 175.0 - Body mass index: 18.0 ← persisted via bodyMassIndexUuid ``` ## Related Issue Part of the reference ranges work under [O3-4585](https://openmrs.atlassian.net/browse/O3-4585). Depends on the `1.8.0-SNAPSHOT` bump in openmrs/openmrs-distro-referenceapplication#1004 and, for the criteria-based ranges to actually be evaluated by the backend, on the demo content update Ian Bacher flagged in openmrs/openmrs-content-referenceapplication-demo#63. ## Other - Unit tests updated in `biometrics-overview.test.tsx` and `vitals-biometrics-form.test.tsx` covering: BMI persistence on create, void-and-replace on edit when weight/height change, and `NumericObservation` receiving the right `conceptUuid` / `interpretation` / `patientUuid` for each column. - Weight, height, and MUAC cells are now also styled via `NumericObservation`. Today this means they pick up interpretations the backend already sets; no behaviour change for concepts without reference ranges loaded.
